decisions.executionNote: Begin right-arm approach to mouse, raising and pitching the open gripper gradually while preserving elbow-up continuity.
Advance above mouse with open right gripper and progressively turn downward; estimate grasp location from calibrated head view.
Lower right gripper over mouse while completing downward orientation; keep open until side alignment is visible.
Close around mouse after a short descent, then test retention with a small vertical lift.
Mouse did not clearly rise. Reopen and correct toward its wrist-image position, accounting for a lower tabletop than initially estimated.
Refine mouse centering, descend slightly, close fully and lift to verify retention visually.
Mouse appears between fingers after lift. Keep closed, raise clear of the table and translate toward the pad on the right.
Center the retained mouse over the pad, lower to support, release, and lift clear.
Mouse is released on pad. Withdraw right arm and prepare both hands for a balanced keyboard push, staying on their respective sides.
Move closed grippers toward the keyboard front edge, with left and right contact points separated and matched forward tilt.
Align both closed fingertips just in front of the keyboard at table-edge height before a synchronized forward push.
Gently push keyboard forward with two separated contact points, adding slight rightward alignment and clearance from the table.
Continue a slow forward-right keyboard push toward the outlined frame, keeping left contact on the left side.
Complete a short balanced push toward the frame while maintaining a left/right separation near the centerline.
Keyboard now overlaps the frame. Back both hands away and open, then clear space for the left-arm figurine grasp.
Raise left fingers over the keyboard toward the figurine; withdraw the right arm toward its origin with an open gripper.
Approach the figurine torso with the left gripper open and finish settling the right arm near its origin.
Close the left gripper around the figurine torso and perform a short lift to check that the base rises with it.
The figurine did not rise; reopen and lower the left fingers toward its torso while advancing slightly, avoiding a high empty grasp.
Grasp the now-centered figurine torso, hold closed, and lift vertically for a retention check.
Figurine retention remains unconfirmed. Reopen and correct rightward and lower toward its torso instead of grasping above it.
Close around the lower torso now between the fingers and lift a few centimeters to test figurine retention.
Test whether the figurine follows a small leftward lift toward its stand; keep closed and verify from the next view.
The figurine did not follow cleanly. Reopen, lift clear, and change to an overhead approach instead of continuing the uncertain side grasp.
Replan after continuity rejection: use smaller forward/down increments while completing the overhead gripper orientation.
After the IK interruption, hold orientation and move slightly back/down and toward the visible torso, remaining left of the centerline.
Lower the open left gripper toward the figurine's narrower lower body, using short increments and avoiding further sideways pushing.
Recenter the open fingers toward the visible torso while staying left of center, then close without forcing a large descent.
Keep the figurine gripped and translate left with a small lift toward the visible stand, checking that its base follows.
Figurine follows the gripper. Center its base over the stand, lower to support, open, and begin clearing away.
Large residual suggests contact near the drawer. Back the left wrist away and reduce downward tilt with the gripper open before repositioning.
Regrasp the figurine from the front with a small centering correction, then lift and shift a short distance toward the stand while keeping the wrist clear.
The last side grasp missed. Reopen and move lower and slightly forward/right to bring the narrower torso within the actual fingertip depth.
Close at the newly aligned torso contact and lift leftward a short distance, avoiding further descent into contact.
The figurine base now aligns with the stand. Lower gently to support, release, and back away without lateral disturbance.
Leave the released figurine on its stand and withdraw the open left hand to begin an overhead approach to the alarm clock.
Center above the clock and lower the open left gripper while completing a near-vertical grasp orientation.
Correct clock centering between the fingers, close around its sides, and lift slightly to check retention.
Clock appears retained. Lift it clear of the drawer front while moving left toward the drawer's top, maintaining the closed grasp.
Raise the retained clock above drawer-top height before advancing across its front edge.
Replan after IK continuity rejection: use much smaller rises and relax the downward wrist pitch while retaining the clock.
Advance the retained clock over the drawer top with small upward and forward increments, maintaining clearance and configuration continuity.
Avoid the high forward reach that failed IK. Hold wrist position nearly fixed and reduce its downward pitch to bring the clock forward over the drawer.
Move the clock farther over the drawer while lowering toward its top; retain it until support and placement can be checked.
Set the clock onto the drawer top, open the gripper, and withdraw backward/upward to verify that it remains supported.
Clock is released on the drawer. Retract the left arm clear of the organized objects and begin returning both open hands to origin.
Continue the open-handed return toward origin, lowering only after clearing the drawer and figurine.
